subject: history_social
notes: The Hanseatic League was a network of merchant groups and trading towns in northern Europe.
It was most powerful from the 1200s to the 1400s.
Its member towns, led by Lübeck in what is now Germany, lay mostly along the North Sea and the Baltic Sea.
League merchants traded goods such as fish, timber, grain, and furs.
The league held its last general meeting in 1669.
stem: The student wants to introduce the Hanseatic League to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Led by Lübeck, in what is now Germany, the league's member towns lay mostly along the North Sea and the Baltic Sea.
choices.B: The Hanseatic League, which held its last general meeting in 1669, had been most powerful from the 1200s to the 1400s.
choices.C: Merchants of the Hanseatic League, whose towns lay mostly along the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, traded fish, timber, grain, and furs.
choices.D: The Hanseatic League was a network of northern European merchant groups and trading towns, most powerful from the 1200s to the 1400s.

explanation.why: An audience that has never heard of the Hanseatic League first needs to know what it was. Only one choice explains that it was a network of merchant groups and trading towns and places it in northern Europe at a particular time.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It refers to "the league" as though readers already know what it is, and it never explains what the league was.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It gives dates for the league but never says what kind of organization it was, so an unfamiliar reader would be lost.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It tells where the league's towns were and what its merchants traded, but it never explains what the league itself was.
explanation.D: Correct. It defines the league, says where it operated, and tells when it was most powerful.
